statement: Explicit CNF Davis-Putnam elimination with the first parity-chain auxiliaries eliminated before input variables has exponential output on a linear-clause unsatisfiable width-three family.
hypotheses: n>=3; two XOR chains encoding opposite parity on common inputs; distinct auxiliary variables; explicit non-tautological resolvents and duplicate elimination, optional syntactic subsumption only.
definitions: One XOR gate is encoded by one clause for each forbidden assignment. Eliminate a variable by resolving opposite occurrences and retaining unaffected clauses.
source_locators: Davis and Putnam, J ACM 7 (1960), 201-215; MathOS PNP-002; standard XOR encoding.
proof_or_gap: The first chain projected onto n input variables is even parity. Every non-tautological parity implicate contains all n variables, and exactly one forbidden assignment is excluded per such clause. The second chain remains untouched and cannot syntactically subsume input-only clauses. Thus at least 2^(n-1) clauses of width n appear; summing the original XOR equations proves UNSAT in linear row operations.
implication_to_claim: Eliminates polynomial total bit complexity for this specified explicit representation/order, not for arbitrary SAT algorithms.
unproved_dependencies: A uniformly polynomial alternative representation or unrestricted lower bound.
adversarial_findings: An XOR-aware solver avoids this blowup. General semantic simplification and different variable orders are not covered.
